text:
Recent work supports separating preference polarity from factual support. [Disentangling Likes and Dislikes (2024; revised 2025)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.13248) evaluates whether recommendation explanations align with user sentiment, beyond textual similarity. [GenAudit (2024)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.12566) links supported claims to reference evidence and revises unsupported claims; [QASemConsistency (2024)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.07473) decomposes text into minimal propositions, reporting annotation agreement κ>0.7. These suggest auditing each feedback reason separately, with exact source spans, rather than judging an entire explanation at once.

Proposed adaptation: record user/item IDs, selected/rejected status, original rank, verbatim feedback, reason category, title/description offsets, and evidence status: supported, contradicted, or insufficient information. Categories can include feature match, explicit specification conflict, redundancy, and missing information. Compatibility conflicts require both an explicit requirement and a conflicting specification; absent specifications mean insufficient information. Interaction history alone establishes neither ownership nor satisfaction. Ownership, unmet needs, and diversity/conformity traits remain unknown without direct evidence. Double-annotate cases independently; report raw agreement, Cohen’s κ for reason/evidence labels, span-overlap F1, and adjudicated disagreements. This is a proposed protocol, not an established recommendation taxonomy.

For the twenty users, report case-level selected–rejected rank inversions: among explicitly compared pairs, count cases where a selected item originally ranked below a rejected item, with ties and unranked items separate. Keep these diagnostics separate from macro validation HR@10. A [2026 study](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ijhcs.2025.103720) found persuasive explanations can shift choices toward lower-utility options, reinforcing that selection does not establish factual correctness. Treat this small sample as case analysis, without population-level preference estimates.
